main.t: One of two small bones that form the bridge of the nose (nasal bone).

simpler.t: The nasal bones form the hard top of your nose.

deeper.t: They also support the cartilages that form the sides of the nose.

facts.t: The two nasal bones meet in the midline at the bridge of the nose.
They form the bony base of the nose, above its cartilages.

simpler.t: Feel the hard top of your nose: those are the nasal bones.

deeper.t: Below them, the nose is shaped by cartilage, which is not seen in a dry skull.

items.name: Midline joint
items.t: The two bones meet each other in the midline.

items.name: Bridge of the nose
items.t: Together they form its bony base.

items.name: Lower edges
items.t: Support the cartilages of the side walls of the nose.

items.name: Upper and side edges
items.t: Meet the frontal bone above and the maxillae at the sides.

simpler.t: They are two small bones side by side at the top of the nose.

deeper.t: As facial bones, they are joined to their neighbours by sutures.

facts.t: Together they form a firm bridge that holds the shape of the upper nose.
They support the softer cartilages of the side walls of the nose.

simpler.t: They give your nose a firm top and hold up its softer parts.

items.name: Other nasal bone
items.t: Its partner, meeting it in the midline.

items.name: Cartilages of the nose
items.t: The side-wall cartilages rest on them.

items.name: Septal cartilage
items.t: Forms the front of the nasal septum and separates the nostrils.

items.name: Frontal bone and maxillae
items.t: Meet them above and at the sides.

simpler.t: They meet each other in the midline and hold up the cartilages of the nose.

facts.t: Like the other flat bones of the face, it forms directly from membrane (intramembranous ossification).
facts.check: OpenStax 6.4 says the flat bones of the face form from membrane, but 7.5 says the facial bones form from cartilage; which applies to the nasal bone needs an approved source.

facts.t: The flat bones of the face are the last to ossify from membrane. They reach adult size at the end of the adolescent growth spurt.

items.damaged: The nasal bones break: these are the bones damaged when the nose is broken.
items.cannotDo: Keep the nose straight: the bridge may be pushed to one side.
items.why: The thin bones form the bony bridge, so a blow drives them sideways or inwards.
items.check: OpenStax says these bones break in a broken nose; displacement of the bridge is not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20).

items.injury: A broken nose with a swollen, blocked nostril.
items.damaged: Blood collects under the lining of the septal cartilage (septal haematoma).
items.cannotDo: Breathe through that side of the nose.
items.why: The cartilage depends on that lining for nourishment, so trapped blood threatens it.

items.q: Explain why a broken nose is usually a break of the nasal bones.
model: The nasal bones form the bony bridge of the nose.
They are small and project at the front of the face.
The rest of the nose is cartilage, which bends rather than breaks.
So a blow breaks the nasal bones.
items.check: That cartilage bends rather than breaks is not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20).

items.q: Compare the bony and the cartilage parts of the nose.
model: Bone: the nasal bones form the bridge.
Cartilage: plates form the side walls and the front of the septum.
The bones support the side-wall cartilages.
Cartilage is not seen in a dry skull.

items.q: Predict why a skull in a museum seems to have no nose.
model: Only the nasal bones, at the bridge, are bone.
The rest of the nose is cartilage.
Cartilage is not found in the dry skull.
So a large opening is left below the nasal bones.

check.stem: How many nasal bones are there?
check.why: Two small nasal bones join to form the bridge of the nose.

check.stem: What do the nasal bones support?
options: The cartilages of the side walls of the nose
check.why: They support the cartilages that form the lateral walls of the nose.

check.stem: Which bones are damaged when the nose is broken?
check.why: The nasal bones are damaged when the nose is broken.
